assessment.summary: The findings support two cross-cutting hardening opportunities: one execution policy for every transport, and domain-owned authorization before content and community sinks.

nonNegotiables: Preserve public REST tool names and response shapes.
assumptions: No measured latency or memory budget was supplied.
The plugin should remain deployable without a new service.
Anonymous WooCommerce cart operations may be intentional and require a product decision.

opportunities.title: One policy boundary for REST and native execution
opportunities.summary: Make request, identity, authorization, quota, idempotency, audit, and dispatch controls common to every tool entry point.
opportunities.diagnosis: REST routes and native Abilities duplicate execution paths, while idempotency is claimed after the side effect and the global limiter is shared before authorization.

evidence.claim: Native Abilities call tool callbacks without the REST request-size and rate-limit path.
A shared global bucket is charged before capability and nonce checks.
Security policy ownership is split across adapters rather than enforced by one execution boundary.

desiredInvariants: REST and native invocations use the same policy sequence.
Budgets are isolated by principal and tool.
Idempotency is atomically claimed before a mutation.
Native mutation Abilities require an explicit equivalent policy.

options.title: Local guards and shared atomic utility
options.summary: Patch each current entry point and centralize only atomic counters and idempotency records.

findingCoverage.rationale: The native wrapper must invoke the shared controls.
Principal-aware buckets replace the pre-auth shared budget.

tradeoffs.assessment: The three observed paths are closed, but future entry points can still omit the utility.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise REST, native, and every registered mutation path.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds bounded cache operations without a process hop.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark p50/p95 latency and cache operations.

tradeoffs.assessment: Uses bounded transient records per request/key.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak PHP memory and transient cardinality.

tradeoffs.assessment: Atomic claims prevent duplicate mutation retries.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run concurrent request tests and cache-backend matrix.

tradeoffs.assessment: Principal/tool counters make abuse diagnosis clearer.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify audit and 429 metrics in staging.

tradeoffs.assessment: Keeps current registry and public routes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run response and capability compatibility tests.

residualRisks: A later entry point can bypass the utility.
Atomic cache support varies by deployment.

workPackages: Add atomic idempotency and principal-aware quota helpers.
Wrap native execution with the helpers.
acceptanceCriteria: Anonymous traffic cannot exhaust authenticated capacity.
migrationNotes: Retain existing route names and response shapes.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable the new wrappers only after retaining the tactical checks.

options.title: Unified ExecutionPolicy boundary
options.summary: Route REST and native adapters through one normalized policy and dispatch service.

findingCoverage.rationale: Quota selection and authorization order are centralized.
Idempotency is a policy stage before dispatch.

tradeoffs.assessment: New transports inherit the policy by construction, reducing control drift.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Assert all registered transports call the policy in contract tests.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds normalization and policy dispatch but no network hop.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare p50/p95 latency and callback throughput.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds a bounded invocation context.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak PHP memory under concurrent requests.

tradeoffs.assessment: One failure policy simplifies denial and replay behavior, while migration adds adapter risk.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run status/error compatibility and rollback drills.

tradeoffs.assessment: Central audit and policy reasons improve diagnosis.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify metrics by tool, principal class, and decision.

tradeoffs.assessment: Requires a two-phase adapter refactor and compatibility fixtures.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Ship behind a feature flag and compare legacy/policy decisions.

residualRisks: Host-provided endpoints outside the plugin can still bypass plugin policy.

workPackages: Define normalized invocation and policy result contracts.
Move REST adapters behind the policy.
Move native abilities behind the policy.
acceptanceCriteria: All tool transports share policy decisions.
No mutation executes without an atomic idempotency decision when a key is supplied.
migrationNotes: Keep legacy route names and preserve opt-in native mutation behavior.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable policy adapter registration while retaining Option 1 guards.

opportunities.recommendation: Use the unified boundary as the target design and ship local atomic guards first as the release gate.

opportunities.title: Domain-owned authorization before content and community sinks
opportunities.summary: Make WordPress visibility and BuddyPress/BuddyBoss posting policy explicit instead of relying on a generic capability.
opportunities.diagnosis: The content adapter treats published status as public and the community adapter treats the generic WebMCP gate as sufficient for a domain mutation.

evidence.claim: Published post content is returned without public-visibility or password checks.
Activity creation calls bp_activity_add() after only generic capability/nonce checks.
The adapter lacks a domain policy owner that can evolve with host-plugin versions.

desiredInvariants: Content is publicly viewable, password-allowed, and membership-allowed before serialization.
Community publication passes deployed BuddyPress/BuddyBoss policy checks.
Mutations use a dedicated configurable capability.

options.title: Adapter-local domain guards
options.summary: Add core visibility/password checks and explicit community permission checks in current callbacks.

findingCoverage.rationale: The content callback gets direct WordPress visibility checks.
The community callback enforces a dedicated capability and host policy.

tradeoffs.assessment: Closes the reviewed content and activity paths immediately.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run protected-post and community-policy fixtures.

tradeoffs.assessment: Core checks are local; host policy calls may add lookups.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark content and activity requests with plugins active.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new retained state is required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak memory for collection and activity requests.

tradeoffs.assessment: Failing a policy check prevents the sink, but host-version differences can cause false denies.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test absent and present integration APIs.

tradeoffs.assessment: Existing logs remain, but deny reasons should be made observable.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review production support requirements for policy denials.

tradeoffs.assessment: Small callback changes and capability mapping are reversible.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Check existing role behavior and response compatibility.

residualRisks: Future adapters can duplicate or omit guards.

workPackages: Add dedicated community capability and host policy checks.
acceptanceCriteria: Blocked/suspended community users cannot publish through WebMCP.
migrationNotes: Document capability assignment for existing installations.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert the local checks only after disabling affected tools.

options.title: Domain policy services
options.summary: Expose content and community policy services that compose WordPress, PMPro, and BuddyPress/BuddyBoss decisions.

findingCoverage.rationale: The content policy owns the core and PMPro checks.
The community policy owns controller/hooks and capability decisions.

tradeoffs.assessment: Domain policy becomes reusable across REST, native, and future transports.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Require policy-service contract tests for every integration version.

tradeoffs.assessment: Service dispatch is small, but host policy checks may add queries.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark with query logging and representative membership/community data.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds bounded policy context objects.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak memory under collection and mutation load.

tradeoffs.assessment: Fail-closed policy results are consistent, but version adapters require fixture coverage.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test missing APIs, denied decisions, and controller failures.

tradeoffs.assessment: Stable decision reasons support supportability and audit.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify metrics and admin diagnostics across integrations.

tradeoffs.assessment: Requires integration matrix, service interfaces, and staged adapter migration.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run side-by-side decisions before flipping the service path.

residualRisks: A policy service can still be incorrectly implemented for a host-plugin version.
Custom hooks may intentionally alter access after the service decision.

workPackages: Implement content and community policy adapters.
Migrate existing callbacks and add version fixtures.
acceptanceCriteria: All transports obtain domain decisions from policy services.
Unavailable integration APIs fail closed for protected operations.
migrationNotes: Start with staging shadow decisions and retain local guards.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable service adapters while retaining Option 1 guards.

opportunities.recommendation: Ship local domain guards immediately, then adopt policy services once supported BuddyPress/BuddyBoss versions are covered by integration fixtures.

openQuestions: Which WordPress 6.9+ native Abilities and REST exposure modes are enabled in production?
Which BuddyPress/BuddyBoss versions and posting-policy hooks are supported?
Is the deployment object cache atomic for add/increment operations?
Are anonymous WooCommerce cart mutations intentionally public?
